resources.string: A floating overlay that shows the app in front — and kills it

How it works: the overlay floats on top of whatever app is open and shows its name and package, updated about once a second. "Kill" force-stops it once, as root. "Spam Kill x100" force-stops it 100 times in a row so it stays dead even if it tries to restart itself. Drag the overlay by its header to move it out of the way.

Root (su) is required — without it nothing can be killed, and Start stays disabled. Draw-over-apps permission is also required for the overlay to appear. Usage access is only a fallback for finding the foreground app if the root detection ever fails.

It never kills itself. Everything else — including system apps — is fair game, so be careful what is in front when you tap Kill.
